top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) rests on a distinct physical principle, the magic-wavelength cancellation of light shifts that lets many neutral atoms be interrogated free of Doppler and recoil shifts. It has been independently reproduced in several laboratories, and the two-name allocation with a citation separating it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes is clean and mature. I defer to atomic physicists on the 1e-18 uncertainty figures, but the whole committee supports this slate item and no award would be worse than a sound, confirmed discovery.
